I hear you. I'm on your side. But there is no such thing as a voice associated with a specific race. And there's no 100% way to tell someone's race online unless they disclose it or you see them. I'm contesting your blanket statement and not the racism you're facing. I typically get the reverse from you: "you don't sound like you belong to this race, you sound like you belong to that race." And that's 100% based on my background and where I grew up.

Dialects, colloquialisms, slang, cultural influences all affect how someone sounds. There's no real evidence of a characteristic physiological voice produced by people of different races. What differences there are, physiologically, are more than overwhelmed by age, health, and the deliberate use of the social voice.

In summary: There are many people who "sound like they belong to one race" but aren't actually from that race. So basing race off voice alone is not proof of who is perpetuating racism.

1. The biggest issue, as has already been pointed out, is anchoring all of your furniture to the wall. 2. There are usually three different types of rug setups in a living room: all furniture on the rug, front legs on the rug, or all furniture off the rug with a coffee table to balance the dead space in the middle. That rug is seriously awesome, but is so far from the rest of your furniture that the only practicality it serves is comfort when you do yoga.

3. Your room height looks to be much taller than the standard height you'll find in most apartments or homes, so this following point may just come down to personal taste. Curtains are typically mounted closer to the ceiling to make the room appear taller and thus bigger. This room is already huge, so you don't necessarily need to employ this illusion. However, I've often found that curtains mounted closer to the ceiling and wider than the window frame almost always look better. From the photo, the low entertainment unit and curtains truncate this side of the room a little. If you raised the mounted rods a bit and replaced the curtains with ones that are longer (textured or patterned), it would create less of a solid blocky feel on that wall.

Misting is not a valid concept!

This is a myth!

Misting provides humidity for maybe five minutes until it dries up. It absolutely has no effect on the plant long term and has been proven over and over again. Five minutes of temporarily improved humidity doesn't give the plants enough time to open their stomata.

In many, probably more than half of all plants, exposure to rain causes rapid suppression of photosynthesis by inducing stomatal closure and causing temporary decrease or cessation of the photosynthetic mechanism. Examining plants exposed to several minutes of misty rain often reveals complete stomatal closure within two minutes, with a 30-40% decrease in photosynthetic ability within one hour. In addition, it often takes many hours to several days for plants to return to a "pre-rain" ability to carry on the efficient business of photosynthesis.

Unless you have a machine spraying mist on them periodically throughout the day, there is no residual benefit other than the placebo effect of being a good caretaker. Misting does help keep plants clean, however.
